rfi.title: Russia accuses France of direct involvement in Ukraine war following RFI report
rfi.description: Russia has accused France of direct involvement in the war in Ukraine, after an RFI investigation revealed that French soldiers have been secretly operating in Ukraine since at least the summer. The reaction from Moscow comes as a defence analyst warns the revelations could fuel Russian propaganda and political tensions in France.

rfi.title: Le Pen to end France’s financial aid to Ukraine if elected president
rfi.description: Marine Le Pen on Monday said that France would provide no further financial aid to Ukraine if she is elected president next year, after a meeting with Kyiv's ambassador in Paris.

rfi.title: EU economics chief warns France and Belgium must reduce deficit and public debt
rfi.description: France and Belgium must bring down their public debt and deficit levels, European Union economy chief Valdis Dombrovskis warned on Tuesday as he unveiled the European Commission's autumn economic forecast.

rfi.title: 'A message to drug gangs': life sentences for 'barbaric' Marseille murders
rfi.description: Two leading figures in Marseille's drug-trafficking underworld were sentenced to life imprisonment on Monday for a triple murder in 2020. Anti-drugs activist Amine Kessaci, whose brother was among the victims, hailed the verdict as a "message to the narcocracy".

rfi.title: Two years after arrest of Uganda opponent Besigye, family raises health concerns
rfi.description: On 16 November, 2024, Ugandan opposition figure Kizza Besigye was arrested in Nairobi, Kenya. Two years on, his wife Winnie Byanyima is calling for his release so that he can receive specialised medical care.

rfi.title: Five EU member states open talks with Rwanda on deportation centre
rfi.description: Austria, Germany, the Netherlands, Denmark ​and Greece are jointly spearheading a project to deport migrants to centres outside Europe and have selected Rwanda for an initial pilot project, scheduled to open next year.

rfi.title: ’Time for another voice’: Diallo launches campaign to dethrone Fifa boss Infantino
rfi.description: Philippe Diallo, head of the French Football Federation, on Tuesday officially launched his campaign to replace Gianni Infantino as president of the game's world ruling body Fifa with a call for change following a series of scandals that threatened to tear apart the 122-year-old organisation.

rfi.title: French presidential candidates clash over tax, housing and the minimum wage
rfi.description: Five candidates for the 2027 French presidential election on Monday evening wrangled over issues including the cost of living crisis, the minimum wage and single parents in a live televised debate.

rfi.title: France braces for second nationwide strike over demands for higher wages
rfi.description: France is braced for its second nationwide strike in less than a fortnight on Tuesday, after unions called on nearly six million public-sector workers to take to the streets to demand higher wages.

rfi.title: DRC Ebola outbreak still 'out of control' six months on, Africa CDC warns
rfi.description: Africa's top public health agency has warned that the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo "is still not under control" six months after it was declared, citing deadly attacks on health workers, unpaid staff and a shortage of resources.

rfi.title: EU imposes fresh sanctions on Russia's banks, oil sector and business elite
rfi.description: The European Union on Monday imposed a fresh round of sanctions on Russia, targeting its banking and oil sectors as Brussels steps up pressure on Moscow over the war in Ukraine. Russia's richest woman, Tatiana Kim, was among those blacklisted.

rfi.title: Trump lands in Manila for Southeast Asian leaders’ talks, as France eyes closer ties
rfi.description: Southeast Asian leaders are wrapping up their annual ASEAN summit in Manila on Tuesday, amid concerns over trade disruption, energy insecurity and maritime tensions in the South China Sea.

rfi.title: Cop31 negotiators unveil draft deal as fossil fuel divisions persist
rfi.description: Negotiators at the Cop31 talks in Turkey on Monday published an 18-page draft deal as part of their efforts to narrow the gaps between dozens of countries over the use of fossil fuels and providing money to help poorer countries tackle the effects of climate change.

rfi.title: WHO warns progress on antimicrobial resistance falls short of 2030 targets
rfi.description: Most countries now have national plans to tackle antimicrobial resistance, but few have put the funding in place to implement them, the World Health Organization warned on Monday. The United Nations health agency said the world was falling behind on efforts to contain drug-resistant infections, which threaten millions of lives and could undermine decades of medical advances.

rfi.title: Francophonie summit delays secretary-general vote after Rwanda-DRC deadlock
rfi.description: The International Organisation of La Francophonie has postponed the election of its next secretary-general by one year after members failed to reach a consensus at a summit in Cambodia. The decision follows a bitter dispute between the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Rwanda over the future of incumbent Louise Mushikiwabo.

rfi.title: French actor Depardieu withdraws appeal against conviction for sexual assault
rfi.description: French actor Gérard Depardieu has apologised after withdrawing his appeal against a May 2025 conviction for sexually assaulting two women on a film set.

rfi.title: France boss Zidane hails players after reaching Nations League last eight
rfi.description: France internationals were heading back to their domestic clubs on Monday buoyed by praise from head coach Zinedine Zidane after securing a place in the 2027 Nations League quarter-finals as League A Group 1 winners.

rfi.title: French cybercrime unit probes massive cyberattack on La Poste subsidiary
rfi.description: A French anti-cybercrime unit was on Monday investigating a massive cyberattack which targeted a subsidiary of the La Poste group mid-September. The contact details of 22 million people were exposed during the attack, the Paris prosecutor's office confirmed on Sunday.

lemonde.title: Comment les Ukrainiens ont réussi à détruire une partie du « pont de Poutine » reliant la Russie à la Crimée
lemonde.description: Des drones et des missiles ont ciblé, le 17 novembre, l’une des deux arches de cette mégastructure de 19 kilomètres, qui s’est effondrée dans les eaux du détroit de Kertch. Vital pour la péninsule ukrainienne, cet ouvrage inauguré en 2018 se veut aussi un symbole politique fort pour le Kremlin.

lemonde.title: Manifestations du 17 novembre : de Paris à Lyon, un mouvement qui regarde vers la présidentielle, « on envoie un message au prochain locataire de l’Elysée »
lemonde.description: Mardi, les cortèges ont rassemblé 146 000 personnes dans différentes villes de France, selon le ministère de l’intérieur, plus de 500 000 selon la CGT. Alors que la mobilisation semble s’essouffler, les regards se tournent peu à peu vers le scrutin présidentiel d’avril 2027.

lemonde.title: « Inside Deutsche Bank » : les documents secrets qui lient Donald Trump à l’argent sale azerbaïdjanais
lemonde.description: Pour la première fois, les révélations d’une enquête internationale permettent d’établir un lien formel et direct entre le président américain et l’argent sale azerbaïdjanais.

lemonde.title: Procès des parents de « la petite inconnue de l’A10 » : la mère condamnée à vingt ans de réclusion, le père à quinze ans
lemonde.description: Les deux accusés sont incarcérés immédiatement avec cette décision, qui marque l’aboutissement, trente-neuf ans après les faits, d’un des plus anciens « cold cases » français, objet de plusieurs livres et documentaires.

lemonde.title: En Israël, la police et le renseignement intérieur accusés d’avoir servi le clan Nétanyahou pour contester les résultats des législatives
lemonde.description: Trois semaines après les élections, aucun élément concret ne vient étayer les accusations de « fraude massive » portées par le premier ministre, Benyamin Nétanyahou, et relayées par la police et le Shin Bet à l’encontre des listes arabes. Ces allégations avaient conduit à des perquisitions et des placements en garde à vue.

lemonde.title: « Jupiter » : la vertigineuse solitude du président face à l’arme nucléaire, incarné à l’écran par Denis Ménochet
lemonde.description: Le réalisateur Alexandre Smia fait monter la pression dans un huis clos au sein duquel le chef de l’Etat français doit décider d’utiliser ou non la bombe atomique contre la Russie.

lemonde.title: Au procès de l’explosion de la rue de Trévise, le « combat acharné » des associations de victimes face à la « maltraitance institutionnelle »
lemonde.description: Linda Zaourar, présidente de l’association des Victimes et rescapés de l’explosion de la rue de Trévise, et Dominique Paris, de Trévise Ensemble, ont exposé à la barre, mardi 17 novembre, leur lutte pour une juste indemnisation des victimes.

lemonde.title: L’évocation de la vie privée de la militante Anne-Cécile Mailfert en direct sur Franceinfo vire au débat politique ; la chaîne présente des excuses et plaide la transparence
lemonde.description: Lundi, à la fin d’un débat consacré à Gérard Depardieu et à la question des violences sexuelles, une journaliste a invoqué la charte déontologique de la chaîne publique pour rappeler qu’Anne-Cécile Mailfert est la compagne d’un dirigeant de France Télévisions.

lemonde.title: Royaume-Uni : une réforme « radicale » pour remettre dans l’emploi « une génération perdue »
lemonde.description: Un rapport a été publié, mardi, qui propose des mesures pour les près d’un million de jeunes Britanniques âgés de 16 à 24 ans qui ne sont ni en emploi, ni en études, ni en formation. Le gouvernement s’en inspirera pour présenter ses propositions en 2027.

lemonde.title: Cancer du pancréas : la Commission européenne donne son feu vert à un nouveau traitement
lemonde.description: L’essai clinique mené par Revolution Medicines, la biotech américaine à l’origine du daraxonrasib, montre un doublement de la survie médiane chez les patients l’ayant reçu.

lemonde.title: Logement : l’Assemblée vote un amendement du RN supprimant toutes les interdictions de location liées au DPE
lemonde.description: Les députés sont allés plus loin que le texte initial, qui prévoyait déjà un assouplissement de la réglementation sur les passoires énergétiques, en supprimant toutes les interdictions de louer liées au diagnostic de performance énergétique.

lemonde.title: Présidentielle 2027 : Gérald Darmanin appelle Bruno Retailleau et Gabriel Attal à s’effacer derrière Edouard Philippe, pour barrer la route à Jean-Luc Mélenchon
lemonde.description: « Si M. Mélenchon est au second tour face à Mme Le Pen, je pense que ce sera un choc immense dans notre pays », a déclaré mardi le ministre de la justice, estimant que le candidat « insoumis » l’emporterait dans une telle configuration.

lemonde.title: « Un abandon flagrant de responsabilité et d’humanité » : HRW dénonce le projet de cinq pays européens d’expulser des migrants vers le Rwanda
lemonde.description: L’Allemagne, l’Autriche, le Danemark, la Grèce et les Pays-Bas ont présenté un projet inédit visant à transférer vers le Rwanda des demandeurs d’asile dont les recours ont été définitivement rejetés.

lemonde.title: L’Iran a « utilisé le prétexte » de la guerre au Moyen-Orient pour « intensifier la répression », dénonce Amnesty International
lemonde.description: Raha Bahreini, chercheuse principale de l’ONG pour l’Iran, rapporte que le nombre d’exécutions pour des motifs politiques a augmenté « à un niveau jamais vu ces dernières décennies » dans le pays, avec au moins 39 personnes exécutées en lien avec les manifestations antigouvernementales de janvier.

lemonde.title: Prostitution des mineurs : un rapport parlementaire appelle faire peser la charge de la preuve sur les « clients pédocriminels »
lemonde.description: Le rapport, rédigé par la délégation aux droits des enfants de l’Assemblée nationale, propose de légiférer sur « la plus grosse défense » des clients pédocriminels, qui affirment penser que la personne prostituée avait déclaré être majeure au moment des faits.

lemonde.title: Produits défrisants accusés de causer des cancers : L’Oréal conclut un accord avec quatre plaignantes aux Etats-Unis
lemonde.description: Le montant de l’indemnisation de ces quatre femmes afro-américaines n’a pas été rendu public. Le groupe français, qui défend la sûreté de ses produits supposés lisser les cheveux, fait face à de nombreuses plaintes de clientes américaines.

france24fr.title: Le conseil d'administration de Nvidia ferme la porte à un retour de son ex-patron Jensen Huang
france24fr.description: "Le conseil d'administration de Nvidia a accepté à l'unanimité sa démission et n'envisage pas de réinstaller Jensen au poste de directeur général", a assuré mardi son président Harvey Jones, qui a dit vouloir trouver un remplaçant à cette figure de l'IA "aussi vite que possible." Le géant affiche une santé de fer au troisième trimestre avec des perspectives relevées.

france24fr.title: Une primaire de la droite et du centre prend forme avec les équipes d'Attal, Retailleau et Lisnard
france24fr.description: Réunis mardi, les représentants des candidats à la présidentielle Gabriel Attal (Renaissance), Bruno Retailleau (LR) et David Lisnard (Nouvelle Energie) se sont mis d'accord sur le principe d'une primaire à deux tours, organisée d'ici fin janvier. Ils la veulent "la plus ouverte possible", y conviant Édouard Philippe, tout en excluant les candidats de partis "extrêmes", "selon Renaissance.

france24fr.title: Scandale Nvidia : comment les réseaux pro-Pékin utilisent l'IA pour manipuler l'affaire Jensen Huang
france24fr.description: Depuis la démission fracassante du fondateur de Nvidia sur fond d'affaire d'espionnage au profit de la Chine, la machine à désinformation tourne à plein régime sur les réseaux sociaux. Et la plupart utilise ce que Huang a contribué à créer : l'IA. De faux audios de son épouse aux memes viraux, décryptage d'une campagne propagée par des comptes pro-Pékin, alors que Donald Trump entame une tournée asiatique en pleine course à la domination technologique dans le secteur de l'IA.

france24fr.title: CAN 2027: en attendant le verdict du TAS, le Maroc bat le Niger et rejoint le Sénégal parmi les qualifiés
CAN 2027 : en attendant le verdict du TAS, le Maroc bat le Niger et rejoint le Sénégal parmi les qualifiés
france24fr.description: Le Maroc n'a pas été brillant face au Niger mais la victoire (1-0) à domicile, mardi, a suffi. Assurés de participer à la CAN 2027, les Lions de l'Atlas rejoignent le Sénégal parmi les qualifiés, comme champion ou vice-champion en titre, selon la décision à venir du TAS concernant la finale de l'édition 2025.

france24fr.title: 🔴 Israël : Matan Kahana, un fidèle d'Eisenkot, élu président du Parlement
Israël : Matan Kahana, un fidèle d'Eisenkot, élu président du Parlement
france24fr.description: Matan Kahana, ancien militaire proche du centriste Gadi Eisenkot, a été élu mardi à la tête du parlement israélien. Un revers pour le camp de Benjamin Netanyahu, dont l'opposition entend rapidement détricoter l'héritage législatif.

france24fr.title: CAN 2027: le Burkina Faso valide son billet et celui du Bénin, le Mali et le Cameroun qualifiés
france24fr.description: Pluie de qualifications à la CAN 2027 dans les matches de la soirée de ce mardi 17 novembre. Le Mali est allé gagner au Rwanda (2-0) pour décrocher son billet. Le Burkina Faso a fait de même avec une victoire 3-1 contre la Mauritanie, qui profite mathématiquement au Bénin. Les Étalons et les Écureuils sont ainsi les deux qualifiés du groupe F. Tandis que le Cameroun se qualifie sans jouer à la faveur de la victoire des Comores contre le Congo-Brazzaville (1-0).

france24fr.title: Que fait le Salvador en Haïti ?
france24fr.description: Les Nations unies ont appelé mardi 17 novembre les forces de sécurité en Haïti à donner la priorité à la protection de la population. Plus de 2 000 soldats salvadoriens ont été déployés en Haïti fin octobre pour secourir quatre aviateurs qui faisaient partie d'une force internationale de lutte contre les gangs et qui ont disparu après une attaque près de la capitale Port-au-Prince.

france24fr.title: COP31: un projet de déclaration finale qui fait polémique
france24fr.description: À la COP, les ministres de l'environnement négocient la déclaration finale. Le projet de texte reprend toutes les propositions des différentes parties et se contredit parfois. Une exhaustivité contre-productive qui pourrait conduire à un échec des négociations. L'Union Européenne, par la voix de son commissaire au climat, se dit prête à renoncer à la mention de l'origine décarbonnée de l'électricité dans le paragraphe sur l'électrification, dans le but de trouver un accord.

france24fr.title: "Fractures françaises" : jusqu'où ?
france24fr.description: La mobilisation se poursuit en France : les fonctionnaires ont battu le pavé dans plusieurs villes du pays pour réclamer une hausse des salaires face à l’inflation. Des lycéens et des étudiants étaient également présents dans les cortèges. Selon la CGT, 500 000 personnes ont manifesté à travers la France, dont 175 000 à Paris. De son côté, le ministère de l’Intérieur estime le nombre de manifestants à 146 000, dont 28 000 dans la capitale.

france24fr.title: Francophonie : face à l'impasse, l'élection du secrétaire général repoussée d'un an
france24fr.description: L'élection du secrétaire général de l'Organisation internationale de la Francophonie (OIF), au coeur d'un bras de fer entre République démocratique du Congo et Rwanda, a été reportée d'un an lundi faute de consensus, un "compromis" diversement accueilli. La sortante rwandaise Louise Mushikiwabo, qui a dénoncé des "pressions nombreuses et fortes" à son encontre, restera en place jusqu'à la tenue du nouveau scrutin, auquel le Rwanda ne présentera pas de candidat.

france24fr.title: CAN 2027: l'Algérie s'écroule au Togo, la Tunisie ne gagne toujours pas
france24fr.description: L'Algérie avait besoin d'une victoire pour espérer une qualification dès la 4e journée de ces éliminatoires de la CAN 2027. À la place, les Fennecs se sont complètement écroulés au Togo (3-0). La Tunisie, qui avait besoin de gagner pour se relancer et prendre confiance, a fait match nul contre la Libye, sur fond de polémique pour un penalty sifflé trop généreusement.

france24fr.title: CAN 2027: la Sierra Leone retarde la qualification de la RD Congo, la Côte d'Ivoire freinée par la Gambie
CAN 2027 : la RD Congo retarde sa qualification, la Côte d'Ivoire ralentie en Gambie
france24fr.description: La Côte d'Ivoire et la RD Congo avaient besoin d'une victoire ce mardi 17 novembre, respectivement contre la Gambie et la Sierra Leone, pour valider leur billet pour la CAN 2027. Le travail n'a pas été fait. Les Léopards ont concédé le nul en toute fin de match (1-1). Les Éléphants, eux, se sont fait surprendre par les Gambiens après avoir mené au score (2-2) et voient le suspense relancé dans leur groupe.

france24fr.title: Comment une fausse citation de Christine Lagarde a été amplifiée par un réseau de désinformation srilankais
france24fr.description: Selon plusieurs publications Facebook, Christine Lagarde aurait déclaré que "les personnes âgées vivent trop longtemps", ce qui représenterait un "risque" pour l’économie. Une fausse citation attribuée à tort à la présidente de la Banque centrale européenne, actuellement relayée par un réseau de désinformation basé au Sri Lanka.

france24fr.title: Record du monde : Nataliia Zharkova plonge en apnée à 124 mètres  de profondeur
france24fr.description: Nataliia Zharkova plonge à 124 mètres et établit le record de profondeur en apnée féminine. Dans la catégorie “poids constant” où l'Ukrainienne concourt, les plongeurs descendent et remontent sans s'aider d'une corde, tout en étant soumis à une pression intense sur leurs poumons, à des besoins en oxygène accrus et à un long parcours à la nage pour regagner la surface.

france24fr.title: Guerre en Ukraine : une partie du pont de Crimée s’effondre après des frappes de Kiev

letemps.title: Reconstruire l’Etat en profondeur après les élections de mi-mandat
letemps.description:
OPINION. Démantelée par Elon Musk et son Département de l’efficacité gouvernementale, l’administration américaine a perdu bon nombre de fonctionnaires, et sa mémoire institutionnelle au passage. Sa reconstruction pourrait désormais bénéficier d’une conjoncture favorable avec un Sénat démocrate, écrit Daniel Warner

Les démocrates sont sortis des élections de mi-mandat avec un mandat, mais sans

spiegel.title: Amazonasregenwald in Brasilien: Isoliert lebende Awá-Indigene tauchen in Dorf auf
spiegel.description: Die Rede ist von einer »historischen Begegnung«: Im brasilianischen Amazonasregenwald haben sich etwa 20 Mitglieder des Awá-Volkes kurzzeitig aus ihrer Isolation begeben. Die Hintergründe sind alarmierend.

spiegel.title: Donald Trump: Technikprobleme in Serie – Kritik in eigenen Reihen wächst
spiegel.description: Bemerkenswert leichtfertig tut Donald Trump die Ausfälle bei Banken, Behörden und im Flugverkehr ab. Aber selbst enge Vertraute geben sich damit nicht mehr zufrieden. Der Druck auf den US-Präsidenten wächst.

spiegel.title: Wayne Rooney über psychischen Tiefpunkt: Düstere Jahre bei Manchester United
spiegel.description: Als der englische Fußballstar Wayne Rooney bei Manchester United spielte, war das eine der besten Phasen seiner Karriere. Privat sah es zur selben Zeit aber extrem düster aus, wie er nun erzählt.

spiegel.title: Nvidia will Jensen Huang nicht als Chef zurückholen
spiegel.description: Die Rückkehr von Jensen Huang an die Nvidia-Spitze ist laut Verwaltungsrat vom Tisch, obwohl er dazu bereit wäre. Derweil boomt das Geschäft des Chipriesen weiter.

spiegel.title: Vertrauter von Eisenkot: Israels Opposition übernimmt Parlamentsvorsitz
spiegel.description: Ein Politiker der Opposition ist in Israel zum Vorsitzenden des Knesset gewählt worden. Matan Kahana ist Mitglied derselben Partei wie Gadi Eisenkot – doch für den bleibt die Regierungsbildung ein Drahtseilakt.

spiegel.title: Christian Sewing: Wie sich der Deutsche-Bank-Chef an die Spitze kämpfte
spiegel.description: Das Datenleck bei der Deutschen Bank enthüllt, wie sich Konzernchef Christian Sewing an die Spitze kämpfte. Aus einem Mann, der einst streng auf das Einhalten von Regeln achtete, ist ein Manager geworden, den Vorschriften nerven.

spiegel.title: »NSA Net«: Internes Netzwerk von US-Geheimdienst NSA gestört
spiegel.description: Die Serie technischer Defekte und Ausfälle in den USA geht weiter. Dieses Mal ist die geheime interne Kommunikation der NSA betroffen. Auch der Techkonzern Apple meldet Störungen bei mehreren Onlinediensten.

spiegel.title: Anthropic-Börsengang: »KI-Firmen arbeiten wie Goldminen«, sagt Analyst Benedict Evans
spiegel.description: Anthropic steuert auf einen billionenschweren Börsenstart zu, oder platzt die KI-Blase? Der prominente Techanalyst Benedict Evans spricht über nervöse Märkte und späte Gewinner des KI-Booms.

spiegel.title: Siedlungspolitik: Großbritannien verhängt Sanktionen gegen israelische Baufirmen
spiegel.description: »Kein Geschäft mit der Zerstörung der Zweistaatenlösung«: Die britische Regierung geht mit Sanktionen gegen die illegale israelische Siedlungspolitik vor. Ziel sind mehrere Firmen in Großbritannien.

spiegel.title: Ukraine-Krieg: USA kritisieren ukrainische Angriffe im inneren Russlands
spiegel.description: Bei einem Treffen von Verbündeten der Ukraine haben die USA Manöver der Ukraine scharf kritisiert. Boris Pistorius gibt Kyjiw Rückendeckung und nennt die Vorwürfe »dumm«.

spiegel.title: Gerald Knaus über Return Hubs in Ruanda: »Den Tausenden, die jeden Monat kommen, muss die Überfahrt sinnlos erscheinen«
spiegel.description: Können Abschiebungen ins ferne Ruanda Europas Problem mit irregulärer Migration lösen? Der Experte Gerald Knaus befürwortet ein Abkommen mit dem afrikanischen Land. Moralische Bedenken lässt er nicht gelten.

spiegel.title: Niedersachsen: Justizministerin Wahlmann gerät wegen verschwundener Akte in Bedrängnis
spiegel.description: Eine Akte mit Ermittlungsergebnissen zu einem korrupten Staatsanwalt soll in Niedersachsens Justizministerium monatelang nicht auffindbar gewesen sein. Die Aussage eines Abteilungsleiters bringt Ministerin Kathrin Wahlmann nun in Bedrängnis.

spiegel.title: Rätsel des Alltags: Warum haben Landtiere stets eine gerade Anzahl an Beinen?
spiegel.description: Von der Ameise bis zum Elefanten – sie alle haben eine gerade Anzahl an Beinen. Wozu? Ein Foto-Stativ kann ja schließlich auch auf drei Beinen stehen. Was sich die Natur dabei gedacht hat.

spiegel.title: Ruanda-Deal: Dieser Mann kann kein Partner sein – Meinung
spiegel.description: Deutschland und vier weitere EU-Staaten wollen abgelehnte Asylbewerber nach Ruanda schicken. Möglich, dass die Gerichte diese Idee durchwinken. Beschämend ist die Aufwertung des Autokraten dennoch.

spiegel.title: Unicef: Bundesregierung will Svenja Schulze als Chefin vorschlagen
spiegel.description: Deutschland plant, sich um den Chefposten des Uno-Kinderhilfswerks zu bewerben. Über die Kandidatur der ehemaligen Ministerin soll SPIEGEL-Informationen zufolge das Kabinett entscheiden.

spiegel.title: Augsburg: 15-Jährige verletzt Mädchen mit Messer
spiegel.description: Erst streiten sie, dann sticht eines der beiden Mädchen zu: In Augsburg hat eine Jugendliche zwei Menschen verletzt, ein Opfer ist erst 14 Jahre alt. Die mutmaßliche Täterin sitzt in Untersuchungshaft.

spiegel.title: Infantino-Herausforderer Philippe Diallo: Ein Held ist, wer antritt, obwohl er chancenlos ist
spiegel.description: Die Uefa hat doch noch einen Gegenkandidaten für Fifa-Boss Gianni Infantino gefunden. Der Verbandsfunktionär Philippe Diallo geht in ein aussichtsloses Duell. Das ehrt ihn.

spiegel.title: Alexander Zverev: Ex-Freundin Brenda Patea hat Klage gegen Tennisstar eingereicht
spiegel.description: Brenda Patea hat Alexander Zverev vor Jahren körperliche Übergriffe vorgeworfen. Verurteilt wurde der Tennisprofi nicht. In einem Interview sagte er, seine Unschuld sei bewiesen. Nun geht sie dagegen vor.

elpais.description: Los días van pasando en el hospital. Mi madre, María Luisa, sigue sin admitir ningún tipo de alimento. Le quitan también el suero porque le está hinchando las piernas. La dosis mínima de morfina hace que cada vez le cueste más mantenerse despierta y cuando lo está es con enorme esfuerzo. Vuelve a repetir “esto es lo que yo no quería”

elpais.description: Los retratos de 600 mujeres de las élites muestran cómo la representación del cuerpo de la mujer europea ha ido menguando y alejando visualmente de su función reproductora

elpais.description: Robert Pattinson se suma a un grupo que ha ido de Sean Connery a Daniel Craig, pasando por George Lazenby, Roger Moore, Timothy Dalton y Pierce Brosnan

elpais.description: A dos días de su estreno en el teatro con público, el actor, sus compañeros de escenario y su mentor y director Juan Carlos Corazza presentan ante la prensa ‘¡Chéjov! ¡Chéjov!’

elpais.description: El presentador dice que lo que se descartó de la entrevista a Santiago Abascal es menos que lo que quitaron a Pedro Sánchez y no cambiaría el sentido: “Ya hicimos una excepción y la cagamos. Nos la liaron”

nyt.title: After Days of Digital Outages, Americans Wonder if the Country Is Breaking
nyt.description: The digital outages that began on Thursday may not be linked, but they have left Americans with a sense that the nation is off-kilter, with no one ready to fix it.

nyt.title: A.I. Helps Find Major Security Bug in Java, a Software Platform Vital to the Internet
nyt.description: The discovery by security company Calif shows A.I.’s ability to find gaping security holes in popular software. The Java flaw pointed to vulnerabilities in systems used by nearly all Fortune 500 companies.

nyt.title: Apple Addresses Outages Affecting Apple Pay, iCloud and Apps
nyt.description: The disruption followed days of unrelated problems in the past week that interrupted air travel and work at offices, schools and government.

nyt.title: Iran Is Emboldened After Trump and GOP’s Election Losses, Officials Say
nyt.description: Iran’s negotiating position has hardened since the midterms, U.S. and other Western officials say. An American lawmaker warned that Iran felt “strategically empowered.”

nyt.title: Nvidia Has No Plans to Bring Back Jensen Huang
nyt.description: As the former chief executive and his allies lobbied for his return, the company’s chair said the board “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as C.E.O.”

nyt.title: Measles Is Officially Back
nyt.description: Also, public schools are closing as enrollment drops. Here’s the latest at the end of Tuesday.

nyt.title: For Democrats, a Leadership Fight Is Marring an Electoral Triumph
nyt.description: The contest between Senators Chuck Schumer and Chris Van Hollen to be majority leader is sowing party divisions and putting them on public display.

nyt.title: With House Democratic Majority Still Growing, Recounts Are Starting in Closest Races
nyt.description: The exact size of the Democratic majority in Congress was undetermined as recounts were sought in two races in North Carolina and one in Minnesota two weeks after the elections.

nyt.title: Hakeem Jeffries Embraces Medicare Expansion on Eve of Speaker Vote
nyt.description: The top House Democrat endorsed lowering the eligibility age, covering all children and adding vision, hearing and dental services, proposals seen as precursors to Medicare for All.

nyt.title: Will a Spy Scandal, Trade Friction and a Surprise Guest Ruin Xi’s Big Moment?
nyt.description: The leader wants the APEC summit to showcase China’s strengths, but he faces export worries and an unpredictable Trump, who has floated meeting Kim Jong-un.

nyt.title: U.S. Loses Its Measles Elimination Status, a Historic Setback for American Health
nyt.description: The nation was once regarded as a global leader for reining in the highly contagious virus. Now, large outbreaks that sicken thousands could become routine.

nyt.title: 26 More Measles Cases in New York, but Outbreak Appears to Be Easing
nyt.description: The state has recorded over 270 cases this year, the most since a major outbreak of the illness in 2018 and 2019. More than two dozen cases were recorded this past week.

nyt.title: Democrats Assail RFK Jr. After U.S. Loses Measles Elimination Status
nyt.description: Incoming senators and prospective presidential candidates blamed the health secretary’s history of vaccine skepticism for the rise of measles in the country.

nyt.title: Do You Need a Measles Booster?
nyt.description: As cases spread across North America, now is a good time to check your vaccination status.

nyt.title: Markwayne Mullin Defends Flight to L.S.U.-Texas Game After Ground Stop
nyt.description: “We still gotta live our lives,” said the homeland security secretary, who is required to use government planes for personal travel. His department said he paid.

nyt.title: Hegseth Nominates His Former Aide to Lead the Army
nyt.description: After months of delay, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and the White House have sent Gen. Christopher LaNeve’s nomination for Army chief of staff to the Senate.

nyt.title: Does This Man Have a Right to the Data From His Own Brain?
nyt.description: J. Galen Buckwalter cheerfully agreed to provide his neural data for a research study. But when he asked for a copy, things got complicated.

nyt.title: Matan Kahana Elected Speaker of Israel’s Parliament
nyt.description: Matan Kahana, a lawmaker from Gadi Eisenkot’s party, will take control of the legislative process as the opposition looks to press Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on multiple fronts.

npr.title: Xi said China would welcome American students for exchanges. What's the reality?
npr.description: President Trump and China's leader Xi Jinping are due to meet in the Chinese city of Shenzhen. At their last summit in September, Xi said he will welcome 100,000 American students for exchanges.

npr.title: Iran launches a third round of strikes on Bahrain, host of U.S. Navy's 5th Fleet
npr.description: Iran fired drones on Tuesday at a U.S. radar facility in Bahrain, and the U.S. retaliated by firing at Iranian targets along an important shipping route.

npr.title: Trump is in Asia ahead of Xi, Putin summit. And, tech leaders want Huang back at Nvidia
npr.description: Trump says he plans to discuss Ukraine during his Asia trip, which contradicts what the White House previously announced. And, Silicon Valley leaders are pushing for Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia.

npr.title: Trump arrives in Philippines to kick off Asia trip
npr.description: Manila is President Trump's first stop on a three-day trip that will later take him to China for historic three-way nuclear talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.

npr.title: Ukraine strikes major Russian bridge with drones and missiles as aerial attacks escalate
npr.description: Ukrainian drones and missiles struck the Kerch Bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimean, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said, as Russia reported its forces downed Ukrainian drones.

npr.title: Trump to meet Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin for joint summit
npr.description: President Trump is off for a series of meetings in Asia that will cover trade, security and a rare trilateral meeting with China and Russia.

npr.title: Africa: Trading in yuan
npr.description: The dollar has long ruled Africa's financial landscape. But as more countries turn to China's yuan, the balance of economic power could be shifting.

npr.title: U.N. talks seek to rein in 'killer robots' as fears over AI weapons grow
npr.description: Countries are meeting in Geneva to negotiate rules on weapons that can select and kill targets without human intervention. But with the U.S., Russia and Israel resisting legally binding controls, campaigners fear the window to act is closing.

npr.title: FAA ground stop still affecting thousands of flights. And, Trump meets Xi, Putin in Asia
npr.description: U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said that things could be back to normal at the end of Monday after an FAA ground stop disrupted flights. And, Trump heads to Asia for a high-profile trilateral summit.

npr.title: Chris Van Hollen says he can beat Chuck Schumer. Here's his case
npr.description: Sen. Chris Van Hollen told NPR's Morning Edition why he believes he can defeat Sen. Chuck Schumer and what he would change about Senate Democratic leadership.

phys-org.title: How restaurants can make sustainable dining choices easier while still making a profit
phys-org.description: Canadians are eating out less. A 2025 survey found 57% of them are cooking at home more often to save money, while 69% of restaurant operators say customers are dining out less because of affordability. According to Restaurants Canada, 41% of operators are either losing money or breaking even.

phys-org.title: Writing as it should be or as it sounds: Reconstructing how Old English disappeared
phys-org.description: In the twelfth century, the English-speaking world underwent a major change: Old English gave way to Middle English. In his dissertation, Ph.D. candidate Amos van Baalen uses sermons to reconstruct how this change took place.

phys-org.title: How much CO₂ will stay? New study estimates long-term residual emissions under the EU Emissions Trading System
phys-org.description: Current CO₂ emissions covered by the EU Emissions Trading System (EU-ETS1) could be substantially reduced by 2040. A new study by the Oeko-Institut, commissioned by Carbon Market Watch, examines the level of emissions that could remain in 2040 and 2050. In 2040, installations covered by the EU-ETS1—including waste incineration—could still emit between 159 and 231 million metric tons of CO₂.

phys-org.title: How do human lifestyles affect the gut microbiome of our canine companions?
phys-org.description: Dogs have been living side by side with humans for millennia, but a new study underscores how much we have yet to learn about man's best friend. The study, which looked at hundreds of dogs across four nations, found that the lifestyles of pet owners appear to play a significant role in determining what constitutes a healthy gut microbiome for their dog companions.

phys-org.title: How machine learning can tackle lead pipe challenges
phys-org.description: A new machine learning tool developed through the Centre for Resilience in Environment, Water and Waste (CREWW) could help water companies identify properties most likely to be connected to lead service pipes.

phys-org.title: Study tracks what students learn from online teamwork and fieldwork abroad
phys-org.description: Can a solution that cuts food waste in Tokyo work in Seoul too? Exploring a familiar problem with peers abroad can help students question what they take for granted at home and see how their knowledge might apply to real-world sustainability challenges. As educators put time and care into designing international courses, what do students take away from the experience, and what stays with them after the course ends?

phys-org.title: Quantum-gas microscope resolves the 'color' of individual atoms in a single shot
phys-org.description: In 2024, researchers at the Ultracold Quantum Gases group at ICFO built a quantum-gas microscope capable of imaging individual atoms in strontium quantum gases for the first time, marking a key enabling step for quantum simulation. At that time, the researchers imaged strontium-84, a boson that has no spin.

phys-org.title: At base of ocean food chain, scientists uncover impacts of a changing atmosphere
phys-org.description: Much of the concern about elevated levels of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere focuses on its effects on global warming as a greenhouse gas. But up to 30% of emitted carbon dioxide is absorbed by the oceans, where it reacts with water to lower pH and leads to ocean acidification, which has enormous effects on the chemistry and biology of marine ecosystems.

Sixteen years later, FIU biologist Shen Jean Lim tested it only to discover the microbes that devoured much of the oil in 2010 were nowhere to be found in 2009. So where did they come from?

phys-org.title: Lasers near physical limits of miniaturization open possibilities for tracking life at the nanoscale
phys-org.description: From tracking how cancer develops to exploring how the brain works, scientists need ways to observe biological processes at increasingly smaller scales. Beyond tracking how cells move and interact, researchers need to understand how tiny structures within cells, including organelles and molecular complexes, behave and change over time. However, identifying and tracking these microscopic targets individually remains a major challenge.

phys-org.title: New model identifies priority areas for large-scale ecological restoration in Chile
phys-org.description: Researchers from Chile's Institute of Ecology and Biodiversity (IEB) have developed a multiobjective model to identify priority areas for large-scale ecological restoration in Chile, South America. The tool integrates four ecological objectives: reducing species extinction risk, prioritizing carbon stocks, restoring riparian areas and assessing ecological feasibility. phys-org.description: Te Whare Wānanga o Waitaha | University of Canterbury (UC) botanist professor Pieter Pelser has been recognized with one of the highest honors in taxonomy, with a newly established South American daisy genus named Pelseria in acknowledgment of his decades-long contribution to studying the family tree of plants.

phys-org.title: New Asian flying frog species identified in Indonesia
phys-org.description: In the lush mountain rainforests of Indonesia, researchers have identified a new species of Asian flying frog with distinctive physical features, calls and unusual egg-laying habits. The discovery is described in a paper published in the journal Zootaxa by scientists from Museum Zoologicum Bogoriense in Indonesia, the University of California, Davis, and other collaborators.

phys-org.title: Extreme cold preserves passion fruit's vitamin C, but not all of its antioxidants
phys-org.description: Passion fruit can travel thousands of kilometers before it reaches international markets. Along the way, one of the food industry's biggest challenges is making sure its nutritional qualities survive processing, storage and transport.

undark.title: Australia’s Social Media Ban Has Not Worked — For Now
undark.description: New data coming out of Australia suggests that bans alone may not be an effective enough deterrent to stop children from using social media. But the research faces limitations. What does that mean for other countries considering similar restrictions?

undark.title: Body Snatchers and the Murky Process of Whole-Body Donation
undark.description: Opinion | Each year, more than 20,000 people in the U.S. donate their bodies to science after death. But the programs that handle whole-body donations lack oversight, with inconsistencies in standards of consent, transparency, and accountability. The result is reminiscent of the body-snatching practices of years past.

undark.title: Book Review: The Bizarre Frontiers of Product Testing
undark.description: From rampaging bears to zero-G toilets and chicken cannons, Alex Davies, in “Kobuk the Destroyer,” chronicles the surprising and often bizarre world of test engineering, and the ingenious lengths to which product testers will go to make the world a safer place.

undark.title: After Cancer, a Complex Aftermath for Survivors
undark.description: Around 70 percent of people with cancer today will live for more than five years after their diagnosis. They’re likely to find that life after cancer is complicated — marked by health risks and chronic illnesses — and that their primary care doctors may be ill-equipped to help them navigate it.

undark.title: Could an Amazonian Highway Open a Pandora’s Box of Pathogens?
undark.description: Brazil has plans to repave a neglected 550-mile road in the South American rainforest to help connect the region and boost economic growth. But some scientists are concerned the project — which would likely increase access between humans, livestock, and wildlife — might be a biosecurity risk.

undark.title: Interview: The Nerve That Could Transform Medicine
undark.description: Kevin Tracey, a researcher and neurosurgeon whose team discovered the vagus nerve’s link to the immune system more than two decades ago, has developed an electrical implant to stimulate the nerve in an effort to help rheumatoid arthritis sufferers who currently have difficulty taking medications.

undark.title: AI and Virtual Reality Enter the Therapist’s Office
undark.description: Some experts say that deepfake technology and other AI tools could help tackle treatment-resistant conditions like anorexia and prolonged grief. But plenty of questions remain, including whether there could be damaging side effects and whether the therapy is even effective.

undark.title: On the Weather Radar: Cloudy With a Chance of Birds
undark.description: This year’s spring migration in North America unveiled real-time measures at a higher resolution than ever before. On one night, for instance, 156 million birds appeared in the skies, outpacing the forecasted total by 20 million. And researchers figured that out thanks to AI.

undark.title: In a Long-Awaited Move, FDA Enforces Trial Result Transparency
undark.description: After years of limited oversight, the FDA sent warnings to more than 2,200 clinical trial sponsors about missing results, which were supposed to be uploaded to an official public database. Experts have pushed for greater transparency.

undark.title: Book Review: An Optimistic Defense of Uncertainty in Science
undark.description: At an uncertain moment in the sciences, Stuart Firestein argues in favor of optimism in “It Could Be Otherwise,” since uncertainty leaves room for possibility, and possibility drives curiosity, imagination, and the agency to study the peculiarities of the natural world.

proj-syn.title: Nigeria’s Big Bet on Health Care
proj-syn.description: Nigeria’s dependence on imported medicines and medical equipment leaves families exposed to exchange-rate fluctuations and hospitals at the mercy of global supply chains. Expanding domestic manufacturing is essential to reducing the cost of treatment and ensuring that more Nigerians can access quality care.

proj-syn.title: What Should the Nvidia Board Do?
proj-syn.description: The proper role of any corporate board is to strike a careful balance between stakeholders. In Nvidia's case, the board will have to consider not just the current trading price, but also how its decisions will affect the landscape in which it operates, its employees, and its license to trade.

proj-syn.title: The Roots of Macron’s Failure
proj-syn.description: Although French President Emmanuel Macron has certainly made mistakes, his troubled presidency is symptomatic of a deeper problem. In the end, he failed to build something truly enduring because he was seduced by the same monarchical impulse that is a recurring feature of French political culture.

proj-syn.title: Yalta in Shenzhen?
proj-syn.description: In principle, the planned summit of the US, Russian, and Chinese presidents could usefully address what should be done to limit the proliferation of nuclear weapons, ensure that AI is more a force for good than harm, and end ongoing wars and prevent new ones. But principle is one thing; in practice, we are likely to see something else.

proj-syn.title: The Perverse Effects of the AI Investment Boom
proj-syn.description: As big tech companies increasingly turn to debt markets to finance massive investments in AI data centers, they are competing for the same pools of capital as many governments. With interest rates already high and public demands for spending on the rise, the timing could hardly be worse for vulnerable economies.

proj-syn.title: Oceania’s Three Goals for COP31
proj-syn.description: To make COP31 the “Blue COP,” delegates must recommit to keeping the 1.5° Celsius warming goal alive, reform the climate-finance system, and address our dependence on the fossil fuels driving the ocean's warming and acidification. Pacific countries have long championed these causes, but now the rest of the world must join them.

proj-syn.title: America After the Midterms
proj-syn.description: The Democrats came out on top in the midterms by staying on message and focusing on affordability. But from voters’ perspective, there is an enormous difference between repudiating the administration and embracing the alternative.

proj-syn.title: Can Brexit Be Reversed?
proj-syn.description: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has called Brexit a mistake, and opinion polls show that his proposal to "go all the way" and rejoin the European Union has majority support. But Brexit was won by a movement, and only a movement can reverse it.

proj-syn.title: Portfolio Regime Change?
proj-syn.description: Rather than assuming that traditional asset-allocation guidelines apply to current conditions, investors should position themselves for more volatility and uncertainty. The AI revolution and various structural forces mean that there is no going back to the familiar old diversification formula.

proj-syn.title: The Global Economy After the Iran War Ends
proj-syn.description: Even if the Iran war ended tomorrow, the global economy would not simply pick up where it left off. Reopening the Strait of Hormuz could bring down commodity prices and ease inflation, but postwar reconstruction could redirect capital away from the United States, undermining the AI supercycle and fueling de-dollarization.

proj-syn.title: Breaking Billionaires’ Political Grip
proj-syn.description: The US midterm elections showed that despite the outsize role of money in politics, even the biggest donors don’t always get their way. But defeating billionaires at the ballot box won’t stop them from buying political influence as long as the rules permit them to do so.

proj-syn.title: The Dance of Empires
proj-syn.description: Empires have a habit of preparing to fight the last war while their rivals work out how to win the next one. The US is no different, pouring its resources into military adventures while China slowly but steadily reclaims the scientific and technological leadership that once made it the world's greatest power.

proj-syn.title: The Rare-Earth Game
proj-syn.description: China will probably not impose a rare-earth embargo, but it will keep the specter of one alive. And the West will probably not achieve self-sufficiency in this critical sector, but it will keep seeking to reduce its vulnerability to a supply shock through expensive capacity duplication and stockpiles.

proj-syn.title: Why Research Matters
proj-syn.description: Over the past 21 months, in the country that has leveraged research to greatest effect, the government is slashing funding for it, closing centers where it is done, politicizing grant-making decisions, and bullying its single biggest engine: universities. The costs will be far greater than many realize.

proj-syn.title: Africa Needs a Different Kind of Climate Finance
proj-syn.description: Roughly half of the climate finance that flows to Africa comes in the form of debt, with multilateral and bilateral development-finance institutions often lending at commercial rates to economies already struggling to carry the added costs. To maximize fiscal space, the instruments used to deliver climate finance need to change.

proj-syn.title: Effective Climate Action Requires Capable States
proj-syn.description: With delegations from around the world gathering for another international climate conference, the question today is not whether governments should do more to address the climate crisis, but whether they even have the capabilities to do so. After 40 years of free-market orthodoxy, many simply do not.

proj-syn.title: Why Is Mexico Defying Latin America’s Right Turn?
proj-syn.description: How Mexico’s left has managed to retain strong support is a key question of contemporary Latin American politics. The most likely answer centers on the ruling Morena party’s pragmatic brand of left-wing politics, which combines bold redistributive policies, greater security, and a willingness to compromise in the name of both.

proj-syn.title: The Digital-Currency Divide
proj-syn.description: The rush to develop central bank digital currencies has slowed as underwhelming demand and mounting costs have given governments second thoughts. But while the Federal Reserve and other central banks have shelved their plans, the European Central Bank is pressing ahead with its digital euro.
